input.primaryCondition: Newly diagnosed Stage 2 Hypertension in a middle-aged Indian male

opinions.diagnosis: Stage 2 hypertension (BP 158/98 mmHg) with high cardiovascular risk given diabetes. Target BP < 130/80 mmHg.
opinions.treatment: Start ACE inhibitor immediately given diabetic nephropathy risk. Aggressive BP target < 130/80 as per ICMR 2023.
opinions.notes: Strong preference for ACE inhibitor due to renoprotective benefit in diabetic hypertension per ICMR and ABDM guidelines.

opinions.diagnosis: Hypertension Stage 2. Lifestyle modification possible before pharmacological escalation.
opinions.treatment: Start with Amlodipine (CCB) as first line — lower risk of ACE inhibitor cough which is common in Indian patients (up to 40%). Add salt restriction < 5g/day, daily walking.
prescriptions: Telmisartan 40 mg once daily if CCB insufficient at 8 weeks
opinions.notes: ACE inhibitor cough affects 15–40% of Indian patients due to ACE gene polymorphism — prefer ARB or CCB as first line for Indian patients.

citations.title: Safe and unsafe diabetes medications in pregnancy
citations.snippet: In pregnancy, Metformin and Insulin are considered safe for diabetes management. Sulfonylureas (Glimepiride, Gliclazide), SGLT2 inhibitors (Empagliflozin), and GLP-1 agonists (Semaglutide) are NOT recommended during pregnancy. Gestational diabetes target: fasting glucose <95 mg/dL, post-prandial <140 mg/dL at 1 hour.
citations.reference: ICMR Clinical Practice Guidelines for Type 2 Diabetes 2022

citations.title: Antibiotics are NOT indicated for common cold or viral respiratory infections
citations.snippet: WHO guidance clearly states antibiotics do not help and should not be prescribed for common cold, rhinitis, acute bronchitis, or influenza. These are viral infections. Inappropriate antibiotic use contributes to antimicrobial resistance. Treatment is symptomatic: rest, hydration, paracetamol for fever.
citations.reference: WHO Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2015

citations.title: NSAIDs combined with anticoagulants significantly increase bleeding risk
citations.snippet: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Naproxen) combined with anticoagulants (Warfarin, Heparin, or DOACs like Rivaroxaban, Apixaban) significantly increase the risk of serious GI and intracranial bleeding. If analgesia is needed in anticoagulated patients, prefer Paracetamol at standard doses. If NSAID is unavoidable, add a PPI (Omeprazole, Pantoprazole).
citations.reference: WHO Essential Medicines Drug Interactions Reference 2021

citations.title: Metformin is first-line for Type 2 Diabetes in India
citations.snippet: ICMR guidelines recommend Metformin as the first-line pharmacological agent for Type 2 Diabetes unless contraindicated (eGFR <30, hepatic failure, contrast procedures). Start at 500mg once daily and titrate over 4 weeks.
citations.reference: ICMR Clinical Practice Guidelines for Type 2 Diabetes 2022

citations.title: Triple Whammy combination causes acute kidney injury
citations.snippet: The combination of ACE inhibitor (or ARB) + NSAID + Diuretic is called the 'Triple Whammy' and is the most common cause of drug-induced acute kidney injury in India. This combination severely reduces renal perfusion. Stop the NSAID first if AKI develops. Prefer Paracetamol for pain in patients on this combination.
citations.reference: WHO Essential Medicines Drug Interactions Reference 2021
